articleTitle: Persian Sentiment Analysis Without Training Data Using Cross-Lingual Word Embeddings
abstract: In this paper, a low-cost Persian Sentiment Analysis is performed without any Persian training data. A cross-lingual method is proposed to overcome the shortage of labeled Persian Sentiment Analysis datasets by using English as a high-resource language. A cross-lingual model between English and Persian is trained to generate aligned word embeddings that are used as the feature vectors in the sentiment model. Monolingual word embeddings used in cross-lingual approach are English FastText and Persian GloVe. VecMap method is used as the cross-lingual tool to make English and Persian word embeddings aligned in a supervised mode. Furthermore, a 5,000-word English-Persian bilingual dictionary is used as the supervision. Bilingual lexicon induction evaluation reveals that English and Persian are aligned properly in the joint space. The proposed Sentiment Analysis model is trained on an English dataset, and then is tested on Persian using aligned English-Persian word embeddings. The dataset used as the training data is Amazon Fine Food Reviews and Persian Snapp Food dataset is utilized as the test data. The model results show significant efficiency in the Sentiment Analysis task, though it does not use any Persian dataset in training procedure. The proposed cross-lingual Sentiment Analysis shows a good performance with F1-score of 78.16% on Persian test data.

articleTitle: Robust Audio Watermarking Using Graph-based Transform and Singular Value Decomposition
abstract: Graph-based Transform (GT) has been recently leveraged successfully in signal processing domain, specifically for compression purposes. In this paper, we employ the GBT, as well as the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) with the goal to improve the robustness of audio watermarking against different attacks on the audio signals, such as noise and compression. Experimental results on the NOIZEUS speech database and MIR-1k music database clearly certify that the proposed GBT-SVD-based method is robust against the attacks. Moreover, the results exhibit a good quality after the embedding based on PSNR, PESQ and STOI measures. In addition, the payload for the proposed method is 800 and 1600 for speech and music signals, respectively which is higher than some robust watermarking methods such as DWT-SVD and DWT-DCT.

articleTitle: Optically Controlled Reconfigurable Substrate Integrated Waveguide Slot Array Antenna for 5G Applications
abstract: In this paper, a reconfigurable standing-wave linear slot array antenna based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology is presented in 5G frequency band. Both the frequency tuning and the beam shaping can be obtained by incorporating photoconductive switches (PS) in the structure. To this end, a 6-slot SIW array is designed to operate at 29.8 GHz. Then the switches are applied to change the operation frequency to 28 GHz and attain the multibeam functionality. The results obtained by Ansoft HFSS and CST Studio Suite simulators are in close agreement with each other. Furthermore, the analytical results for the radiation patterns show good agreement with the numerical ones.

articleTitle: A Reliability Aware Algorithm for Workflow Scheduling on Cloud Spot Instances Using Artificial Neural Network
abstract: IT infrastructures are rapidly growing due to the increased demand for computing power used by applications. Furthermore, modern cloud data centers are hosting various advanced applications based on the user's needs. The goal of this paper is to maximize the reliability of running workflow applications considering spot instances revocation without imposing fault-tolerance overhead. For this purpose, we use an Artificial Neural Network algorithm (ANN) to define a failure prediction module for the cloud spot instances. Indeed, we introduce a novel workflow scheduling algorithm, named Reliability Aware and modified HEFT (Heterogeneous Earliest Finish Time) for minimizing the makespan of a given workflow subject to a specified reliability of the application. To evaluate our ANN based prediction model, we have used a benchmarking data set. The results of the model training demonstrate that the prediction accuracy is about 96 percent. Our experiments illustrate that although makespan does not improve significantly in all experiments, an acceptable level of reliability is achieved.

articleTitle: Private Classical Information over a Quantum Multiple Access Channel: One-Shot Secrecy Rate Region
abstract: In this paper, the problem of private communication of classical messages over a quantum multiple access channel under one-shot setting is studied. In this regard, we first introduce general quantum multiple access wiretap channel, and then we calculate an achievable secrecy rate region for the main channel. The encoding process follows the combination of the superposition and Wyner wiretap coding schemes, and the decoding technique is based on the simultaneous decoder and convex splitting. At last, we extend the results to the l-user case.

articleTitle: A Graph-based Multi-Label Feature Selection using ant Colony Optimization
abstract: Multi-label classification aims at considering multiple labels for each sample. The main issue of multi-label classifiers is reducing their performances while tackling with high dimensional tasks. Feature selection is a general approach to overcome this issue. This paper proposes a multi-label feature selection approach using ant colony optimization (ACO). The proposed method is a multivariate and filter approach, which integrates the mutual information with ACO to rank features. In the early step of the proposed method, the solution space is converted to a graph where nodes represent features, and each shows the relevancy between its corresponding features. In this paper, the relevancy between features is calculated by using the mutual information theory. Then, a graph of features is generated, and then ants are moved through the graph to weight the features based on their importance. In this paper, a novel measure based on mutual information is used to evaluate solutions chosen by the ants. This means that in this paper there is no need to use any learning model to evaluate the solutions and thus the proposed method is classified as a filter approach. The quality of each solution is added to its corresponding features as their pheromone values. Finally, the final feature set including those features which take high pheromone values will be created. The performance of our method is evaluated by performing a set of experiments on five datasets. The obtained results show the better performance of our method in comparison with the other methods.

articleTitle: Security Framework of IoT-Based Smart Home
abstract: Nowadays, smart home is considered one of the rather prominent applications of the Internet of Things, integrating high-levels of efficiency, home security, energy & cost saving to everyone's life. Despite all the benefits this technology provides, privacy and security are highly concerning issues that require more considerations. IoT-A reference architecture was established to evaluate current sources and protocols, ensuring the compliance of things and protocols, and providing a comprehensive solution for different applications of IoT. This paper was performed to provide a general framework for improving security at all levels of design, implementation, and application of equipment and protocols using the IoT-A reference architecture by addressing security challenges in the Internet of Things and smart homes. This paper employs the term Security Framework to refer to a method for applying all technologies, procedures, software, and other components to provide security in smart homes. This paper has been searched for all vulnerabilities and threats of the reference architecture. In this paper, a model has been proposed to improve reference architecture to meet all security requirements. Considering the theoretical evaluations performed in this paper, the proposed framework, which was created by adding two components of threat and vulnerability management and context management while making some alterations to the authorization component, satisfies an acceptable level of the security requirements of the smart home and enhances the privacy of the IoT-based smart home.

articleTitle: An Analog Demodulation Scheme for Cross-QAM Constellations
abstract: In this paper, we propose an explicit scheme for implementing the fully analog demodulation of cross-QAM (CQAM). The proposed method for threshold estimation can be used in square QAM (SQAM) with an odd number of bits per symbol. Our proposed scheme eliminates the need for an ultra-high-speed analog-to-digital converter (ADC) which, implies intensified power consumption and more complexity over the millimeter-wave (mm-wave) communication. The robustness of the proposed method against analog processing errors has been investigated totally.

articleTitle: Joint Pairing and Resource Allocation for V2X Communications
abstract: The necessity of mobility brings the urgency of communications between vehicles and infrastructures for exchanging information. This network should attain strict requirements such as more reliable channels for vehicle to vehicle (V2V) links while preserve the quality of service (QoS) and performance of cellular users. Thus far, it has been considered, V2V receiver had decided to communicate with a transmitter arbitrarily or with the nearest transmitter. However in this paper attempts to review this assumption and add more potential options to it. For this purpose a joint pairing, resource allocation and power control problem in the context of V2V users is formulated and tried to investigate the best solutions for it. In the following the optimal and sub-optimal solutions are considered based on binary power allocation (BPC) criteria and finally, a joint pairing and resource allocation algorithm based on continuous power assignment is proposed for better performance. Simulation results demonstrate and compare the efficiency of our proposed algorithms.

articleTitle: Compact and Narrow-Band Waveguide Filters Using TM Dual-Mode Cavities for Input Multiplexer in Communication Satellites
abstract: This paper presents a compact and narrow-band filter using TM dual-mode cavities, in Ku-band to be used as a channel filter in IMUX of a satellite transponder. The basic structure is the TM dual-mode cavity. To achieve a compact and high Q resonator, such a cavity exploits a pair of degenerate modes (TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">120</sub>, TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">210</sub>). In this achievement, a single cavity can provide two transmission zeroes besides two poles. The design of a four-cavity filter is reported and compared with the experimental results at 10.97 GHz center frequency with 36 MHz bandwidth. The obtained results satisfy the specification requirements. The agreement between HFSS simulation and the experimental results demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed design approach.

articleTitle: An Energy-Efficient Cell Outage Detection Algorithm for Self-Organizing Networks
abstract: Faults and failures are inevitable in dense heterogeneous wireless networks consisting of a massive number of elements. Automatic management of faulty situations is critical in such complex networks. Among the common network failures, cell outage calls for an especial attention. Automatic and efficient management of cell outage improves users' quality of experience and leads to a significant reduction in operational expenditure (OPEX). Timely and rapid detection of cell outage is the first and somehow the most important step in the cell outage management. In this work, we propose a low complexity and energy efficient cell outage detection algorithm. The proposed algorithm utilizes minimization of drive test (MDT) mechanism to gather users' measurements. Applying outlier detection algorithm followed by a novel localization method, occurrence of cell outage and its location can be determined precisely. Simulation results demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed method in both detection and localization of the cell outage.

articleTitle: Power Allocation for Downlink Training in Cell-Free Massive MIMO Networks
abstract: In this paper, the problem of power allocation in downlink (DL) of cell-free (CF) massive multiple -input multiple -output (MaMIMO) systems is studied. The system consists of a large number of single -antenna access points (APs) that jointly serve a large number of users. In is assumed that the system operates in time division duplex (TDD) mode and downlink pilots are transmitted using beamforming training (BT) method. In this network, we propose a power control scheme that optimally allocates power to data and pilot symbols, considering a total energy budget for each AP. The objective of the power optimization problem is maximizing the minimum achievable rate among the users and the constraint is the total power constraint in each coherence interval. Numerical simulations show that the achievable rate corresponding to each user, employing the proposed power allocation considerably improved compared to the case that of provided with equal power between pilot and data symbols.

articleTitle: An Image Dataset of Vehicles Front Views and Parts for Vehicle Detection, Localization and Alignment Applications
abstract: This paper introduces a dataset of front view car images collected from traffic scenes. Each image contains the bounding box of a vehicle which has cropped manually and accurately. The database also includes the parts corresponding to each frontal view car, i.e. left and right lights, left and right mirrors, grill, license plate, and bumper. In addition to vision-based applications such as object detection, verification, and part-based analysis, our database is specialized for testing and developing of trainable bounding box location prediction algorithms. We used a car localization algorithm for performance evaluation, which resulted in a localization accuracy of 87%. Also, we tested our dataset on Viola-Jones object detector and measured its performance in terms of false positive and false negative rates for images of whole-car as well as each individual part.

articleTitle: A New Architecture for Massive MIMO Testbed Laboratory in 5G
abstract: Massive MIMO (M. MIMO) is one of the main parts in 5G radio sections. It is constituted of a large number of antennas used in the TDD/FDD modes (32, 64 or even more antennas) and is capable to process information very fast. M. MIMO is constituted of high power / speed processors or FPGAs, switches and busses. Existing architectures in many research / university centers is based on a switched hierarchical architecture. In this paper while defining properties and requirements of a M. MIMO testbed and reviewing some M. MIMO architectures, introduce a new MIMO architecture other than switch base one which one of its properties is hardware saving and flexibility.

articleTitle: Enhancing Classification Performance between Different GNSS Interferences using Neural Networks Trained by TAC-PSO Algorithm
abstract: Civil Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receivers are susceptible to various interferences. In recent years, there have been many efforts to counteract these interferences. In this paper, we proposed an extension to the socalled Maximum-Likelihood Power-Distortion (PD-ML) detector, a GNSS authentication technique. Our proposed method differs from the PD-ML detector only in the classification stage and focuses on the classification problem. For the purpose of classification, we have used Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs), which are trained with the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm with Time-varying Acceleration Coefficients (TAC)-PSO, an alternative form of the PSO algorithm, best known for efficiently finding the global optima. Our results from simulation environment showed better classification ability in distinguishing between different interferences and interference-free signals in two classes. We achieved 43% accuracy, especially for multi-path afflicted signals, which is far superior to classification accuracies of previous classification methods. Our proposed classification method comes with more computation complexity in the classification stage.

articleTitle: A Novel Compact Reflectarray Antenna Unit-Cell Operating at 5 GHz
abstract: In this paper, a novel and compact reflectarray unit-cell operating at 5 GHz is proposed. The unit-cell is a combination of printed microstrip patches and dielectric resonator antenna. The size of the unit-cell is about 0.3λ×0.3λ at the center frequency. Full-wave simulation of the unit-cell results in linear and extended phase curves. In addition, we designed an array including 26×26 elements of this kind of unit-cell. The final structure is simulated with CST MWS software and maximum gain of 6.3 dB (5GHz) is obtained. Furthermore, the bandwidth of 1-dB and 3-dB changes in gain is equal to 32% and 40%, respectively. It should be noted that a different unit-cell arrangement is used and cross polarization level is reduced as a result. The efficiency of simulated structure is 67.6% at 5 GHz.

articleTitle: Training Doc2Vec on a Corpus of Persian Poems to Answer Thematic Similarity Multiple-Choice Questions
abstract: This paper reports our improvement over the previous benchmark of the task of answering poetic verses' thematic similarity multiple-choice questions (MCQs). These questions, which frequently appear in the Iranian national university entrance exam, require the test-taker to select the verse which is thematically similar to the stem verse. These questions would test a natural language processing (NLP) model's ability to not only understand, but interpret a poetic verse. In this experiment, we trained a Doc2Vec model on a corpus of Persian poems and proceeded to use the trained model to get the vector representations of the poetic verses. Subsequently, the poetic verse among the options with the highest cosine similarity to the stem verse was selected as the correct answer by the model. This model managed to answer %38 of the questions correctly, which was an improvement of %6 over the previous benchmark. Furthermore, it was observed that the model's approach to answering the questions seemed different from the previous model, as there were relatively few questions that the models had both answered correctly. The ultimate goal of this task is to estimate the difficulty of such questions by using the performance of the models as a feature. The fact that the two models did not behave similarly can prove useful, as the model whose performance has the most correlation with that of a human test-taker can be used for the future task of thematic similarity MCQ difficulty estimation.

articleTitle: Broadband Tunable Terahertz Polarization Converter based on Graphene-Shaped Metasurfaces
abstract: In this paper, a broadband tunable polarization converter based on graphene metasurfaces is proposed. This polarization converter works in the terahertz (THz) frequency region, using the advantage of graphene characteristics to have a tunable frequency response. The designed graphene-shaped periodic structure on top of the substrate is utilized to convert the incident wave polarization to the desired target in a flexible operational band in the THz frequencies. The polarization conversion ratio is more than 0.85 in a wide range of frequencies in the THz band from 4.86 to 8.42 THz (the fractional bandwidth is 54%). The proposed polarization converter is insensitive to the angle of the incident wave up to 40°. Using graphene provides a tunable frequency response without changing the geometry of the designed structure.

articleTitle: Impulsive Noise Removal from Gray-Scale Video Sequences via Adaptive Thresholding
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel method to reconstruct a video sequence corrupted by impulsive noise. Images and videos can become sparse through transformations such as discrete cosine transform, Wavelet, and contourlet. We can employ this redundancy in the images and videos and the sparsity of the impulsive noise in the observation domain to recover the noisy video sequence. By introducing the augmentation of the vectorization of frames, we convert the video denoising problem to image denoising and employ the temporal information in our algorithm as well. We then compare our method with the baseline 3-D median filter for random-valued impulsive noise removal from a gray-scale video sequence. Simulation results show that our algorithm is simple and very fast, which makes it a suitable choice for online applications. Moreover, its reconstruction quality is far better than that of the classical method, 3-D median filter.

articleTitle: Scattering Analysis of Periodic Thin Film Sandwiched by Plasmonic Nano-antenna Gratings
abstract: Plasmonic Nano-Antenna Array (PNA) on periodic thin film is analyzed in this paper. Such an inhomogeneous thin film is a periodic structure with two different isotropic materials. Changing these materials leads to obtaining a reconfigurable anisotropic dielectric. This anisotropic dielectric is used as a thin film of a PNA. Such a 2D lattice consists of plasmonic double-square rings shaped nano-antennas. For analysis a complicated structure, the optic axis of anisotropic thin film is chosen to be perpendicular to the PNA's surface. In this analysis, Galerkin version of Periodic Method of Moments ( PMoM) is used in which, the dyadic Green's function is calculated by a model of Transmission Line (TL) by considering the plasmonic effects. Using PMoM-TL approach, the effective surface current densities on nano-antennas are calculated. In the spectral domain, the information of the scattered fields are also evaluated. The analytical results are compared with simulation ones obtained by a commercial FEM based-EM solver for validation. Using such a structure, one can obtain a reconfigurable optical filter without changing the dimensions of the metallization.

articleTitle: SAR Calculation of a Pregnant Woman Model Exposed to LTE and Wi-Fi Signals
abstract: This paper presents a novel Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) calculation for a 43 year-old pregnant woman carrying a 24-week baby. The model is exposed to radiating dipole antennas operating at WiFi and LTE frequencies, which are 5 GHz and 1.8 GHz, respectively. The dipole antennas are designed such that their radiated power equals to the maximum radiated power in WiFi routers and cellphones. The simulations are done in CST software with the radiated power of 23 dBm.

articleTitle: On Multi-Session Website Fingerprinting Over TLS Handshake
abstract: Analyzing Internet users' traffic data and activities has a certain impact on users' experiences in different ways, from maintaining the quality of service on the Internet and providing users with high-quality recommendation systems to anomaly detection and secure connection. Considering that the Internet is a complex network, we cannot disintegrate the packets for each activity. Therefore we have to have a model that can identify all the activities an Internet user does in a given period of time. In this paper, we propose a deep learning approach to develop a multi-label classifier that can predict the websites visited by a user in a certain period. This model works by extracting the server names appearing in chronological order in the TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3 Client Hello packets. We compare the results on the test data with a simple fully-connected neural network developed for the same purpose to prove that using the time-sequential information improves the performance. For further evaluations, we test the model on a human-made dataset and a modified dataset to check the model's accuracy under different circumstances. Finally, our proposed model achieved an accuracy of 95% on the test dataset and above 90% on both the modified dataset and the human-made dataset.

articleTitle: Topological Data Analysis for Classification of DeepSat-4 Dataset
abstract: Topological Data Analysis (TDA) is a new emerging and fast growing field of data science providing a set of tools from algebra, topology, and geometry to extract features from data based on its topological and geometrical features. This paper combines available methods from topological data analysis including persistent homology, persistent entropy, and persistent diagrams to build a strong topological feature extractor model from the topological properties of an image. By feeding features extracted by the topological model to machine learning models, we perform the classification task on DeepSat (SAT-4) dataset.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Reconfigurable Integrated FPGA-based PSK Demodulator
abstract: In this paper, a new approach is presented for design of digital demodulator, which relies on use of highest demodulation order as a platform to simultaneously realize lower order demodulators, with minimum hardware resources and within a single integrated design. In doing so, an 8PSK demodulator is designed and reconfigured to QPSK demodulator by realizing suitable decision block. It is shown that this approach offers the possibility of reducing by about 40% the resource allocation required to implement the decision block. The proposed method can lead to higher performance with lower FPGA resources, meaning that higher number of processing blocks can be used for a given system. Implementation results of the digital demodulator on Virtex-7 485t FPGA from Xilinx are also presented to validate the approach and verify the results. This method can be adapted to other PSK and QAM demodulators as well.

articleTitle: Compact WLAN/C-Band Multiple-Input Multiple-Output Antenna
abstract: Low correlation multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna design for WLAN and C-band is presented in this paper. Two equivalent elements that have a co-plane radiator with microstrip-line and ground plane in the truncated rectangular form are the substructure of this MIMO antenna. Multiple bent stubs are employed to obtain a dual-band function. Low envelope correlation and high isolation between two antenna elements are achieved by placing antenna elements orthogonally. It is reported that the impedance bandwidth less than -10 dB for S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> covers frequency ranges of 2.20-2.91 GHz (710 MHz, 28%) and 6.24-8.82 GHz (2580 MHz, 35%). These spectrums can support systems that use WiBro/WiMAX/ Bluetooth/LTE/WLAN, and C-band. The MIMO antenna has a compact area of 20 mm × 40 mm and it exhibits a stable omnidirectional radiation performance through its working frequency bands. This quality is considered a favorable factor in the industry for relevant requests.

articleTitle: Full-Duplex Radio Frontend Architecture with Enhanced Transmitter-Receiver Isolation
abstract: To overcome the main bottleneck of a circulator-based full-duplex radio frontend, i.e., limited transmitter-receiver isolation, we propose a radio frontend architecture in which the circulator is omitted and two separate orthogonally polarized printed antennas on a common substrate are employed. The transmitter-receiver isolation is further enhanced by patterning the antenna ground plane. The measured isolation for the fabricated frontend amounts to 47 dB for a 2.4 GHz full-duplex system. This can substantially reduce self-interference in a full-duplex communication system.

articleTitle: Measuring Image Blooming using Blurriness Metrics
abstract: Having areas in an image or a video frame with abnormally high light intensity such as including the sun in the frame is oftentimes unwanted. This artefact, however, is sometimes artificially included in an image. Blooming is the computer graphic artefact deployed on bright areas of an image to provide the illusion of extremely bright light. This artefact is often used in cinema post-processing, computer-generated imagery, and video games to produce attraction and real-world sense in the image. Nevertheless, too much blooming is always unwanted. Because of the leakage of light from these abnormally bright areas to neighboring image regions, the edges in these regions get partly faded. Therefore, it is important to measure the amount of blooming in an image or a video stream. In this paper, we propose a method to detect and measure the amount of blooming in an image or a video frame. This technique is based on measuring the sharpness (or conversely, the blurriness) of an image along the edges. The experiments show that the proposed metric can evaluate variations of blooming artifact in an image. Therefore, this measure could be used as an image quality metric.

articleTitle: Area-Efficient Non-Uniform Lowpass Filter Design
abstract: Design and implementation of area-efficient nonuniform lowpass filter based on planar circuit method (PCM) is presented. More specifically, segmentation method is used alongside Green's function method in order to design multi-section transmission line lowpass filters in minimum given area, while achieving superior results compared to conventional techniques based on quasi-lumped elements. Analysis and procedure outlined here lay the foundation for PCM-based synthesis and systematic design of multi-section non-uniform TL LPFs. Results obtained from analysis, full-wave simulations and measurements all confirm the validity and accuracy of the presented approach, which no doubt can offer extra flexibility and freedom in design of similar microwave filters as well as other more complex planar circuits.

articleTitle: An Architecture for National Information Sharing and Alerting System
abstract: Protecting critical infrastructure from cyber threats is one of the most important obligations of governments to ensure the national and social security of the society. Developing national cyber situational awareness platform provides a protection of critical infrastructures. In such a way, each infrastructure, independently, generates its own situational awareness and shares it with other infrastructures through a national sharing and alerting center. The national information sharing and alerting center collects cyber information of infrastructures and draws a picture of national situational awareness by examining the potential effects of received threats on other infrastructures and predicting the national cyber status in near future. This paper represents the conceptual architecture for such national sharing system and suggests some brief description of its implementation.

articleTitle: Statistical Channel Modeling for Long-Range Ground-to-Air FSO Links
abstract: To provide high data rate aerial links for 5G and beyond wireless networks, the integration of free-space optical (FSO) communications and aerial platforms has been recently suggested as a practical solution. To fully reap the benefit of aerial-based FSO systems, in this paper, an analytical channel model for a long-range ground-to-air FSO link under the assumption of plane wave optical beam profile at the receiver is derived. Particularly, the model includes the combined effects of transmitter divergence angle, random wobbling of the receiver, jitter due to beam wander, attenuation loss, and atmospheric turbulence. Furthermore, a closed-form expression for the outage probability of the considered link is derived which makes it possible to evaluate the performance of such systems. Numerical results are then provided to corroborate the accuracy of the proposed analytical expressions, and to prove the superiority of the proposed channel model over the previous models in long-range aerial FSO links.

articleTitle: Integrated Active Diplexer-Leaky Wave Antenna Using Distributed Amplifier and CRLH Transmission Line
abstract: In this paper an S band active diplexer-leaky wave antenna with CRLH transmission line is presented. The proposed structure uses the benefits of nonlinear dispersion relation of CRLH transmission line in distributed amplifier. The structure consists of two active devices at which CRLH transmission lines are connected to the drain of the FETs and conventional microstrip line are connected to the gate of the FETs. The amplified RF signal goes to the CRLH transmission line, which operates as a diplexer and leaky wave antenna. The antenna has frequency beam scanning functionality.

articleTitle: Full Wave Simulation of Antenna Efficiency Characterization by Using a Reverberation Chamber with and Without Reference Antenna
abstract: Antenna efficiency is one of the most difficult parameters of any antenna to measure. One of the practical methods of measuring antenna efficiency is the use of Reverberation Chambers (RC), which increases the accuracy of the measurement. In this paper, based on full-wave simulation of a complete reverberation chamber, the efficiency of a horn antenna is obtained by using two methods, one with the reference antenna and the other one without reference antenna. The results show that by increasing the time of measurement, the accuracy increases dramatically. Simulations show that 25 measurement samples are enough to reduce the error to less than 20%. The comparison also confirms that the first method has more accuracy in this example.

articleTitle: Point-to-Point Threshold Freshness for the Relay Channel: Age of Information Perspective
abstract: This paper will propose a policy and show how our approach works by utilizing a threshold. The threshold is a proper measure for evaluating the amount of freshness of the information. Finding the threshold is a time-consuming and challenging task, and we propose an algorithm to find it based on the Nested Interval Theorem. We have also solved it for some initial points by the Bisection method. Examples and simulation results prove all of our claims as well. Finding the average age for the policy is another innovative task in this paper. We also extend our findings for a network with one relay and show how the relay reduces the average age. All of our works are compared by utilizing the simulation results.

Author Keywords: the freshness of information with relay

articleTitle: Practical Framework for 5G None Stand Alone Deployment: Iran 5G Pilot Case Study
abstract: In this paper a practical framework for 5G none stand alone deployment has been presented and Iran 5G Pilot is considered as a case study. The Iranian first 5G communication pilot has been deployed in Iran Telecommunication Research Center (ITRC) in corporation with MTN Irancell, one of the major MNOs in Iran. The test results show about 1 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> coverage in ITRC, and the test results 1.530 Gbps download data rate, 119 Mbps upload data rate in average. Also electromagnetic radiation intensity of the launched pilot has been measured and monitored live.

articleTitle: Capacity Upper Bound and Minimum Energy-per-Bit for AWGN Relay Channel with Channel Side Information
abstract: In the following paper, we will analyze and study over a subset of channels including relay with channel side information. First, it has been derived an upper bound on the capacity for this AWGN relay channel when the channel side information is non-causally accessible at both, the transmitter and the relay. In the following, a minimization problem for the energy-per-bit for this type of channel has been presented. After that, by using derived results for the capacity of this channel, we evaluate a lower bound for the problem of the minimum energy-per-bit. We investigate that this bound could be less than the bound founded of the classical AWGN relay channels.

articleTitle: A Fast Reliable Technique for Frequency Identification of Generally Lossy Filters via Complex Analysis
abstract: We demonstrate an improved analytical method to derive the critical parameters of generally lossy filters. The technique puts forward feasible solutions to the serious problems of the previous analytic approaches in calculating the admittance/scattering matrix and is in particular useful for high order filters used in satellite communication. The proposed technique benefits from an appropriate accuracy to estimate the unloaded quality factors as well as the global resonances of a filter, even if they are close together. Our method is also very fast in deriving the filter parameters. In addition, the results can be used as a stringent criterion to validate the parameter extraction performed by other parameter extraction techniques. We examine the application of our method in a number of simulated and measured filters in Ku band and compare its results with well-known frequency domain techniques.

articleTitle: Reduction of the Acquisition Time in GPS Receiver by Multi-Stage Frequency Bins
abstract: Acquisition is known as the first part of the software receiver of the Global Positioning System (GPS), which is a challenging part for increasing the speed of the receiver. As a result of the Doppler effect that causes the relative motion between the GPS satellites and the receiver, the frequency of GPS signals can change simultaneously. In this paper, we present a new method to decrease acquisition time. The proposed algorithm divides frequency bins into three stages. Furthermore, at each stage, a new frequency bin is determined and the satellites in Line of Sight (LOS) are detected and separated from the collection list of satellites. To evaluate our proposed method, we utilize two real datasets that were collected from around Iran University of Science and Technology (IUST). The simulation results confirm that the proposed method outperforms the conventional method in terms of the execution time and computational complexity by 34% and 19%, respectively.

articleTitle: MSIoT: Mobile Social Internet of Things, A New Paradigm
abstract: The integration of the social networks system (SNS) with the Internet of things (IoT) introduced a new concept as the Social Internet of Things (SIoT). One of the major challenges in SIoT is the continuous mobility of objects that create temporary social relationships. The relationship topology dynamics cause failure in the complete chain of relationships in SIoT and network navigability, and finally, difficulty in service discovery and composition. Social Internet of vehicular (SIoV) and Mobile Social Network (MSN) are other models that are intended to be similar to SIoT but follow a different path in structure and architecture. This article presents a new paradigm that we named it Mobile Social Internet of Things (MSIoT). This concept eliminates the challenges posed by objects' continuous mobility and encompasses SIoT, SIoV, and MSN patterns. Therefore, its expansion leads to the integration of patterns into a common structure and architecture. Since objects in SIoT, SIoV, and MSN have different roles, first, to integrate these concepts, we present a new classification for objects in these structures, and then introduce the new MSIoT paradigm and define two main components, i.e., Mobility Management (MM) and Service Forwarder (SF). We present four new mobility -friendly social relationships that encompass a large portion of possible social interactions. Finally, using a scenario, we examine how the proposed new components and social relationships behave in MSIoT.

articleTitle: A Variational Auto-Encoder Approach for Image Transmission in Noisy Channel
abstract: Recent advancements in information technology and the widespread use of the Internet have led to easier access to data worldwide. As a result, transmitting data through noisy channels is inevitable. Reducing the size of data and protecting it during transmission from corruption due to channel noises are two classical problems in communication and information theory. Recently, inspired by deep neural networks' success in different tasks, many works have been done to address these two problems using deep learning techniques. In this paper, we investigate the performance of variational auto-encoders and compare the results with standard auto-encoders. Our findings suggest that variational auto-encoders are more robust to channel degradation than auto-encoders. Furthermore, we have tried to excel in the human perceptual quality of reconstructed images by using perception-based error metrics as our network's loss function. To this end, we use the structural similarity index (SSIM) as a perception-based metric to optimize the proposed neural network. Our experiments demonstrate that the SSIM metric visually improves the quality of the reconstructed images at the receiver.

articleTitle: Similarity Preserving Unsupervised Feature Selection based on Sparse Learning
abstract: Various feature selection methods have been recently proposed on different applications to reduce the computational burden of machine learning algorithms as well as the complexity of learned models. Preserving sample similarities and selecting discriminative features are two major factors should be satisfied, especially by unsupervised feature selection methods. This paper aims to propose a novel unsupervised feature selection approach which employs an ℓ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,1</sub>-norm regularization model to preserve global and local similarities by minimizing an objective function. Cluster analysis is also incorporated in this framework to take the inherent structure of the data into account. The experimental results show the strength of the proposed approach as compared with the earlier well-known methods on a variety of standard datasets.

articleTitle: Uncoordinated Channel Tracking for High-Rate Internet of Things in Multiuser Massive MIMO
abstract: The integration of high-rate internet of things (IoT) service into a massive MIMO network is considered. Existing approaches are limited in several ways: i) they incur large overhead for high data rates, ii) they do not consider channel aging explicitly, iii) channel tracking is performed for one device only treating others as noise, iv) pilot access patterns are assumed known at base station (BS) severely limiting network flexibility. Here, several algorithms are proposed that circumvent all of the aforementioned shortcomings with modest complexity. Specifically, ideas from target tracking literature is leveraged to model each unknown pilot contamination pattern as a different target-measurement association. Subsequently, several algorithms based on probabilistic data association filter (PDAF), multiple hypotheses tracking (MHT), global nearest neighbor (GNN), and soft and hard least-squares (LS) are presented. By numerical analysis, it is determined that their performance comes surprisingly close to that of the optimum tracker which knows access patterns when number of BS antennas are large.

articleTitle: Towards Generating Benchmark Datasets for Worm Infection Studies
abstract: Worm origin identification and propagation path reconstruction are among the essential problems in digital forensics. Until now, several methods have been proposed for this purpose. However, evaluating these methods is a big challenge because there are no suitable datasets containing both normal background traffic and worm traffic to evaluate these methods. In this paper, we investigate different methods of generating such datasets and suggest a technique for this purpose. ReaSE is a tool for the creation of realistic simulation environments. However, it needs some modifications to be suitable for generating the datasets. So we make required modifications to it. Then, we generate several datasets for Slammer, Code Red I, Code Red II and modified versions of these worms in different scenarios using our technique and make them publicly available.

articleTitle: Joint User Association and Power-Bandwidth Allocation in Heterogeneous Cellular Networks
abstract: Transmission delay minimization can be considered as an ideal goal for any data transmission system. Regarding the radio resources restriction in cellular networks (e.g. transmit power and bandwidth of base stations (BSs)) delay improvement is taken into account as a complex network optimization problem. Here, the decision process of user association to multiple BSs and traffic load balancing is proposed which improves the resource utilization and establishes the throughput required by each network user with the minimum total average transmission delay. The network to be investigated is heterogeneous cellular network. The average delay is formulated and an optimization problem is proposed to minimize the delay subject to power and bandwidth limitation and also the rate stability condition. This problem is originally nonconvex and a combination of difference of convex method and inner approximation is utilized to convert the problem to a convex form. Various types of user distribution are examined in simulation and the results show significant decrease in system delay average compared to well-known user association approaches such as minimum distance and maximum received signal straight criteria.

articleTitle: Relaxing Pairwise Conditional Dependency of NB Attributes using Hidden Variables
abstract: Conditional independence assumption of naive Bayes classifier as one of its major drawbacks, for real-world applications, has been recently tackled by various structural learning approaches. However, finding the optimal structure is itself reported to be an NP-hard problem. Compliance of the devised structure with general rules and concepts of the literature of Bayesian networks is also another challenge facing many researchers. Eventually, the computational complication of structural learning has impelled many scholars to adopt approaches to confine the search space of possible structures. In this paper, we incorporate a set of hidden variables in a predefined Bayesian network structure, for proposing Pairwise Hidden Naive Bayes Classifier (PHNB). In PHNB, a hidden variable is allocated for each pair of features with conditional mutual information higher than a specific threshold in a diverging connection to preserve their dependency whenever the class variable is instantiated. The Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm is modified using a Bayesian correction approach so as to consider an infinitesimal possibility for unforeseen events while converging to a local optimum. Experiments on 6 UCI benchmark datasets reveal substantial results based on classification accuracy(ACC) and area under the ROC curve(AUC).

articleTitle: Max-Link Relay Selection with Physical Layer Network Coding in Two-Way Relay Networks
abstract: Buffer-aided relaying can considerably increase the reliability of wireless networks. In this paper, we propose a max-link relay selection method with physical layer network coding for wireless two-way relay systems. We derive closed form expression for outage probability both in unlimited and limited buffer size scenarios. Also, we introduce the novel term of relative diversity gain to compare relative advantage of buffer-aided relaying to conventional relaying. Numerical results show that the proposed method achieves better outage performance even with buffer size as small as 2, and reaches diversity gain two times of the number of relays for large buffer sizes.

articleTitle: An Analysis of GitLab's Users and Projects Networks
abstract: GitHub has long been perceived as the exclusive provider of hosting for software development in the minds of many programmers. However, it is far from the only available service out there. GitLab is one of the many platforms offering similar capabilities, which has experienced rapid growth in recent years. GitLab currently holds the second-largest collection of repositories among its competitors. Despite its rapid growth, little attention has been paid to this website by academia. This lack of information with regard to users and projects on the platform, as well as the fast increase in the number of GitLab users motivated us to conduct the current study. In this paper, we perform social network analysis on the data we have collected from the public users and repositories of GitLab. We observe that GitLab is similar to other code-hosting services with regard to its network structure. We also find that the most influential users and projects on the website, are associated with the founding team of GitLab. We further analyze the collaboration and membership networks and, among other things, find that both graphs display high values of assortativity with regard to node degree.

articleTitle: Queue based Resource Allocation for Tactile Services
abstract: In this paper, we study the joint optimization problems to allocate resources for upload and download phases of tactile services which are investigated in cellular networks while queue stability constraint is of interest. In each time slot, the arrival traffic in downlink phase should be proportional to the uplink departure rate at the same time slot, which causes the coupling of the upload and download resource allocation problems. At each upload and download phase, a dynamic resource allocation policy with a stable-queue constraint is proposed to reduce latency. An iterative algorithm for joint power and sub-carrier allocation in both phases of upload and download is designed which is based on Lyapunov drift-plus-penalty algorithm and relaxation method. Via performed simulation under the different system parameters, the performance of the proposed algorithm is evaluated.
